newsitem.title: UK: FULL TEXT - NatWest Markets options statement.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - NatWest Markets options statement.

text.p: The following is the full text of a statement published on Thursday by National Westminster Bank Plc regarding losses in the interest rate options trading book of its investment banking unit NatWest Markets:
NATIONAL WESTMINSTER BANK PLC 13th March 1997 INDEPENDENT FINDINGS OF REVIEW OF NATWEST MARKETS INTEREST RATE OPTIONS TRADING

NatWest Group announced today (13 March 1997) the initial findings of the independent review by Linklaters & Paines and Coopers & Lybrand into the losses that occurred at NatWest Markets in the interest rate options business.
The net charge against pre-tax profits in the first half of 1997 will be 77 million.

The charge of 77 million is higher than the 50 million provision announced on 28 February as a result of a thorough review of the pricing of interest rate option portfolios and of relevant provisioning. The losses have been quantified and the first stage of the investigation has confirmed that they are confined to the interest rate options area.
The procedures adopted by NatWest Markets assisted by KPMG in the revaluation of the portfolios have been reviewed by Linklaters & Paines and Coopers & Lybrand.

The independent review has confirmed that the process adopted by NatWest Markets to establish the extent and timing of the loss, and the valuation methodology applied, was appropriate. The review covered all trading activities in NatWest Markets and other parts of the NatWest Group.

On this basis the charge comprises a reduction of 90 million stg in the book value of certain interest rate option trading portfolios - less relevant provisions of five million stg and the reversal of related unpaid bonuses of eight million stg - giving a net charge of 77 million stg.

The losses relate primarily to 1995 and 1996 since mis-pricing of the portfolios started in late 1994. The calculation of the charge is based on positions in the relevant options book as at 28 February 1997.
MANAGEMENT CHANGES

NatWest Markets has suspended four members of staff and announced the appointment of an acting head of Global Debt Derivatives. The suspensions are part of NatWest Markets' normal investigation procedure and as such carry no implication of misconduct.

Those suspended by NatWest Markets are Ian Gaskell, Head of Swaps Options Trading (UK and Europe), Christophe Lanson, Global Head of Rate Risk Management, Jean-Francois Nguyen, Managing Director, Debt Derivatives and Phil Wise, Chief Administrative Officer and formerly Senior Managing Director, Capital Markets.
Neil Dodgson, Global Head of Options has already been suspended and Kyriacos Papouis, an options trader, left the company on 16 December 1996.
These suspensions have been notified to the SFA.

Peter Hall, President and Chief Operating Officer, NatWest Markets will temporarily take on the additional responsibilities of Chief Administrative Officer. Vincent Tomasi currently Senior Vice President and Head of US Debt Capital Markets at NatWest Markets in New York will take over as acting Head of Global Debt Derivatives.

Separately, with the acquisition of Greenwich Capital and the creation of the Global Debt Markets division, a new management structure for the debt capital markets and specialised finance businesses was planned. This has been accelerated.
BONUS PAYMENTS
As the result of the revaluation bonus payments totalling eight million stg awarded to certain personnel in the Global Debt Derivatives area are now not due and will not be paid.
In addition Martin Owen, Chief Executive of NatWest Markets has decided to forego 200,000 stg of his performance related bonus in respect of 1996.
OTHER FINDINGS OF THE INITIAL REVIEW
There is evidence of losses in certain options books since late 1994. Mis-pricing obscured these losses.
The transfer of value between books also made the losses and mis-pricing more difficult to detect.
The announcement on 28 February was made in order to forestall inaccurate market rumours as soon as the Group believed that it had fairly estimated the extent of the probable loss.

The options and swaptions products traded in NatWest Markets use industry standard models to calculate valuations of the products based on details of the transaction and pricing data. No flaws have been identified in the models.

The second stage of the review being undertaken by Linklaters & Paines and Coopers & Lybrand will also involve the further investigation of the areas where the losses occurred and an investigation of the management issues associated with the deficiencies in these areas.
COMMENT
Commenting on the preliminary report Derek Wanless, Group Chief Executive, NatWest Group said:

"It is extremely regrettable that the losses and the mis-pricing have gone undetected for so long. Although confined to one area this is a significant setback for NatWest Markets. We must continually improve our management and control systems. The lessons learnt from this incident are already being put into practice.
Martin Owen, Chief Executive of NatWest Markets, commented:

"I am very disappointed by the serious deficiency revealed in the interest rate options area. We are making immediate changes. I believe that NatWest Markets has some of the best people to be found in investment banking and we are still on course to achieve our long term financial targets as a global investment bank." Lord Alexander, Chairman of NatWest Group, pledged his continuing confidence in the future of NatWest Markets despite this setback.

"The overall business of NatWest Markets has made great strides in recent years and our commitment to its development into a global investment bank remains unaltered. This incident has rightly caused great concern both inside and outside the bank.
The investigation is independent and thorough and we will not hesitate to take all appropriate action as a result of its findings."
